section_summary: This section (pages 124–203) documents Allied and U.S. State Department efforts in August–October 1945 to locate, secure, and exploit Japanese government records, diplomatic archives, and military-technical intelligence following the surrender of Japan. It opens with extensive USFET G-2 intelligence reports and an in-depth study of captured Japanese correspondence from Berlin detailing German-Japanese technical cooperation in aviation, armaments, and machine tools, as well as the collapsing morale and living conditions of Japanese personnel in Germany. The remainder of the section focuses on worldwide diplomatic maneuvers across neutral and Allied capitals—including Bogota, Havana, Ciudad Trujillo, Ottawa, Vatican City, Beirut, Brussels, Mexico City, Ankara, and Bangkok—to prevent the destruction of Japanese diplomatic archives and negotiate custody among the Four Powers, which remained complicated by delays in directives from General MacArthur's headquarters in Tokyo.

subfiles.about: Catalogues captured papers of the Japanese Naval Attaché in Berlin concerning European war production, naval construction, finance, and intelligence.
subfiles.from: Office of Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2, Headquarters, U.S. Forces, European Theater (Main) (Lt. Col. Dupre Sassard)
subfiles.summary: Japanese naval attaché papers from Berlin, 1943-1945, on European resources, naval construction, anti-aircraft defense and telegrams, sent to MIRS Washington via London.
subfiles.title: Japanese Document Report: Papers of the Japanese Naval Attache, Berlin

subfiles.about: Reports on captured blueprints for German industrial machinery and hydrogenation plants destined for Japan.
subfiles.from: Office of Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2, Headquarters, U.S. Forces, European Theater (Main) (Lt. Col. Dupre Sassard)
subfiles.summary: CD-137: blueprints for motors, an I.G. Farben hydrogenation plant and other technical items seized at the Berlin Embassy in July 1945.
subfiles.title: Japanese Document Report CD-137: Blue Prints for Machinery for Japan

subfiles.about: Details the agreement Aktion 'I.A.' between Germany and Japan returning purchased German armaments and aircraft for European combat use.
subfiles.from: Office of Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2, Headquarters, U.S. Forces, European Theater (Main) (Lt. Col. Dupre Sassard)
subfiles.summary: CD-138: correspondence on the September 15, 1944 'Aktion I.A.' agreement releasing Japanese-bought German aircraft, tanks, flak guns and cannons to German forces.
subfiles.title: Japanese Document Report CD-138: Return of German Armaments bought by Japanese to Germany

subfiles.about: Summarizes captured records documenting Japanese negotiations with German manufacturers for aircraft engines and optical equipment.
subfiles.from: Office of Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2, Headquarters, U.S. Forces, European Theater (Main) (Lt. Col. Dupre Sassard)
subfiles.summary: CD-139: documents on Japanese efforts from 1939 to 1945 to buy Argus engines through Ernst Prieger, the 1941 Sakaraki Commission visit to Goerz, and Zeiss-Ikon optical purchases.
subfiles.title: Japanese Document Report CD-139: Japanese Contacts with German Manufacturers of Air Equipment

subfiles.about: Lists sixteen categories of captured Japanese naval technical documents concerning aircraft, armaments, machine tools, and navigation gear.
subfiles.from: Office of Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2, Headquarters, U.S. Forces, European Theater (Main) (Lt. Col. Dupre Sassard)
subfiles.summary: CD-140: Japanese naval attaché papers on machine tools, aircraft radio and cannons from Oerlikon, Hispano-Suiza and Rheinmetall, engines, fuses, navigation aids and the Sperry bombsight.
subfiles.title: Japanese Document Report CD-140: Aircraft & Equipment - Correspondence with Japanese

subfiles.about: Catalogues forty files of technical reports, purchase records, and intelligence data on German and Japanese aviation spanning 1936 to 1942.
subfiles.from: Office of Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2, Headquarters, U.S. Forces, European Theater (Main) (Lt. Col. Dupre Sassard)
subfiles.summary: CD-141: Japanese naval attaché records on German aircraft production, Heinkel data, Allied aircraft performance, naval supply purchases, Japanese nationals in Berlin and Swiss instruments.
subfiles.title: Japanese Document Report CD/141: Japanese & German Aircraft - Reports and Correspondence

subfiles.about: Inventories Japanese Naval Air Attaché records showing widespread negotiations to purchase machine tools from German and Swiss manufacturers.
subfiles.from: Office of Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2, Headquarters, U.S. Forces, European Theater (Main) (Lt. Col. Dupre Sassard)
subfiles.summary: CD-142: 1941-1943 specifications and correspondence on Japanese purchases of presses, lathes, milling and grinding machines from firms across Germany and Switzerland.
subfiles.title: Japanese Document Report CD-142: Japanese Interest in German Machine Tools

subfiles.about: Details thirty-four captured folders concerning Japanese procurement of German aircraft engines, weapons, electronics, and technical licenses.
subfiles.from: Office of Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2, Headquarters, U.S. Forces, European Theater (Main) (Lt. Col. Dupre Sassard)
subfiles.summary: CD-143: 1940-1943 naval air attaché records on Argus, Daimler-Benz, BMW and Jumo engines, propellers, Oerlikon and Mauser cannons, Zeiss photography, and Fw 200 and torpedo evaluations.
subfiles.title: Japanese Document Report CD/143: Japanese Interest in German Air Equipment

subfiles.about: Summarizes documents and photographs concerning General Tani's mission to the Eastern Front to observe German railway bridge engineering.
subfiles.from: Office of Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2, Headquarters, U.S. Forces, European Theater (Main) (Lt. Col. Dupre Sassard)
subfiles.summary: CD-144: materials seized at Tempelhof on General Tani's mission to the Moscow front, including 1944 railway bridge reconstruction reports, maps and photographs, and a 1938 French aircraft study.
subfiles.title: Japanese Document Report CD/144: Japanese Study of German Bridge Reconstruction

subfiles.about: Provides a detailed inventory of technical files from the Japanese Naval-Air Attaché covering German military aircraft, engines, instruments, and armaments.
subfiles.from: Office of Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2, Headquarters, U.S. Forces, European Theater (Main) (Lt. Col. Dupre Sassard)
subfiles.summary: CD-145: 1939-1945 naval air attaché files on German aircraft and engines, Askania and Contraves instruments, Lorenz and Telefunken radio, bombsights, armament and Allied orders of battle.
subfiles.title: Japanese Document Report CD/145: Documents taken from the Japanese Naval-Air Attache's Office in the Japanese Embassy, Berlin

subfiles.about: Instructs diplomatic missions to prevent the destruction of Japanese archives pending confirmation of Emperor Hirohito's surrender directives.
subfiles.summary: Circular from Byrnes: the War Department asked MacArthur to have the Emperor instruct Japanese missions to surrender archives; meanwhile American representatives should prevent destruction of Japanese archives worldwide.
subfiles.title: Circular Telegram to American Diplomatic Missions on Preserving Japanese Archives

subfiles.about: Reports the Spanish Chargé d'Affaires' intention to transfer intact Japanese archives in Cuba to the Cuban Government.
subfiles.summary: Havana telegram 570: the Spanish Chargé proposes turning Japanese archives over to Cuba on standing instructions; the archives remain intact in sealed boxes.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 570 from Habana regarding Japanese Archives in Cuba

subfiles.about: Informs that Colombian plainclothes police surveillance has been placed inside the Japanese Legation in Bogota.
subfiles.summary: Bogota telegram 1141: Colombia has put plainclothes surveillance inside the Japanese Legation pending the Swiss Chargé's return.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1141 from Bogota on Surveillance of Japanese Legation

subfiles.about: Reports efforts to secure Japanese archives in Bogota and detain a gardener believed to hold key documents, amid Soviet interest.
subfiles.summary: Bogota telegram 1139: with the Swiss Chargé absent, Wiley urges detaining the Japanese gardener holding sensitive records; the Soviet Minister seems determined to keep the archives from American hands.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1139 from Bogota regarding Japanese Archives and Caretaker

subfiles.about: Advises that preliminary inspection shows voluminous Japanese archives in Bogota are written almost entirely in Japanese.
subfiles.summary: Bogota telegram 1149: preliminary report that the recovered Japanese archives are voluminous and almost wholly in Japanese; full report to follow.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1149 from Bogota on Preliminary Examination of Japanese Archives

subfiles.about: Discusses British instructions for joint Allied custody of Japanese archives in Colombia and arrangements to transfer them to the Swiss Legation.
subfiles.summary: Bogota telegram 1146: Britain seeks joint British, American and Soviet custody; the Swiss Chargé approved moving archives to the Swiss Legation, done by truck; efforts to secure the gardener's documents.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1146 from Bogota on Four-Power Custody and Transfer of Archives

subfiles.about: Reports Madrid's authorization for the Spanish Embassy to surrender Japanese archives and property to the Cuban Government.
subfiles.summary: Havana telegram 573: the Spanish Chargé received Madrid's instructions to surrender all Japanese archives and property to Cuba; transfer set for the next day.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 573 from Habana on Spanish Surrender of Japanese Property

subfiles.about: Transmits an Ottawa Embassy memorandum of conversation regarding Japanese property and archives in Canada.
subfiles.summary: Routing slip sending an Ottawa memorandum on Japanese property in Canada to Oscar Straus.
subfiles.title: Routing Slip Transmitting Ottawa Memorandum on Japanese Property in Canada

subfiles.about: Records discussions with Canadian External Affairs regarding protecting powers and custody of Japanese archives in Canada.
subfiles.summary: Robert English reports Canada's Wershoff said Spain asked to be relieved of protecting Japanese interests, Switzerland never took up duties, the Spanish Consul General will surrender files, and Canada awaits legal steps.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation on Japanese Archives in Canada

subfiles.about: Reports the search of the Japanese Legation in Bogota, transfer of key files to the Swiss, and discovery of five locked safes.
subfiles.summary: Bogota telegram 1153: a thorough search of the Japanese Legation moved two cabinet loads of files and films to the Swiss Legation; two truckloads of literature and five locked safes remain sealed.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1153 from Bogota on Search of Japanese Legation and Safes

subfiles.about: Reports the inspection and transfer of Japanese honorary consulate archives in Ciudad Trujillo to the Dominican Foreign Office.
subfiles.from: American Embassy, Ciudad Trujillo (J. F. McGurk)
subfiles.summary: Despatch 306: Japanese honorary consul Menéndez's archives were opened August 31 before US, British, Chinese and Dominican representatives, found of no lasting value, and transferred to the Dominican Foreign Office.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 306: Japanese Government Archives in Ciudad Trujillo

subfiles.about: Analyzes private letters and reports of captured Japanese officials in Germany, assessing their deteriorating morale, wartime hardships, and ideology.
subfiles.summary: This extensive three-part intelligence report examines twenty-six files of correspondence comprising sixty letters written between 1941 and 1945 by twenty-eight Japanese officials, military attaches, and technicians in wartime Germany. Part I presents a topical analysis covering air raid devastation, severe food and consumer shortages, relations with their German hosts, and capital flight remittances to hedge against inflation. Part II provides classified quotations categorized into defeatist sentiments and stubborn determination ('gambari'), illustrating anxiety over Allied advances in the Pacific and in Europe. Part III concludes that by late 1944 most Japanese residents in Germany were gripped by hysteria and privately convinced the war was lost.
subfiles.title: Report on the Examination of Correspondence Taken from Japanese Official Personnel Captured in Germany

subfiles.about: Distributes copies of Ciudad Trujillo Despatch No. 306 regarding Japanese archives to military and intelligence agencies.
subfiles.from: Department of State (FC: Oscar S. Straus)
subfiles.summary: State sends Despatch 306 of September 4, 1945 to MID, ONI, FBI and OSS on disposition of Japanese consular records in the Dominican Republic.
subfiles.title: Transmittal of Despatch No. 306 on Japanese Archives in Ciudad Trujillo
subfiles.to: Military Intelligence Division, Office of Naval Intelligence, Federal Bureau of Investigation, Office of Strategic Services

subfiles.about: Records British Embassy inquiries regarding Allied seizure of Japanese archives and the reported creation of an Allied Council for Japan.
subfiles.from: E. R. Dickover (Office of Far Eastern Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Everson of the British Embassy asks Dickover about Allied procedures for seizing Japanese archives, surprised the US acted without consultation, and queries reports of a four-power Allied Council in Japan.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation on Allied Custody of Japanese Archives and Allied Council

subfiles.about: Inquires whether the Legation in Beirut approves having an OSS representative summarize seized Japanese archives.
subfiles.summary: Acheson tells Beirut the OSS representative can summarize the Japanese archives reported in telegram 274 and asks the Minister's views.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 272 to Beirut on Summarizing Japanese Archives

subfiles.about: Reports joint demarche to the Holy See to prevent destruction of Japanese Embassy archives in Vatican City.
subfiles.from: American Chargé at the Vatican (Harold H. Tittmann, Jr.)
subfiles.summary: Vatican telegram 195: Tittmann sent a note August 31 asking Japanese officials not to destroy or remove Embassy archives; most were probably destroyed; asks whether recovered documents go to Rome G-2.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 195 from Vatican City on Japanese Archives and Vatican Demarche

subfiles.about: Reports taking custody of Japanese archives and consular property in Beirut and requests instructions on inspection.
subfiles.summary: Beirut telegram 274: Wadsworth took delivery for the Four Powers of sixteen sealed cases of archives and personal effects of a Japanese consul who left in 1941, with Lebanese, British and Soviet concurrence.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 274 from Beirut on Surrender of Japanese Archives and Consular Effects

subfiles.about: Transmits Swedish Legation report that no surrender instructions have been received from Tokyo regarding Japanese property in Belgium.
subfiles.summary: Brussels telegram 1132: the Swedish Legation has no word from Tokyo on surrendering archives; Sawyer asks the Department to arrange instructions.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1132 from Brussels on Japanese Property Instructions

subfiles.about: Discusses strategy for securing Japanese archives in Mexico through Mexican custody rather than asserting direct joint Allied possession.
subfiles.summary: Messersmith recommends the Four Powers ask Mexico to seize Japanese archives and share contents rather than insist on joint custody; reports of Japanese diplomats hiding documents with residents.
subfiles.title: Letter from Ambassador Messersmith on Japanese Archives and Property in Mexico
subfiles.to: John W. Carrigan (Chief, Division of Mexican Affairs)

subfiles.about: Informs Embassy Panama that definitive instructions await Tokyo developments and approves local transfer of archives.
subfiles.summary: Acheson tells Panama no conclusive instructions can be given but approves moving seized archives into the Embassy Office Building.
subfiles.title: Telegram to Panama regarding Japanese Archives in Panama

subfiles.about: Confirms the transfer of remaining Japanese archives seized by Panamanian authorities into the American Embassy Office Building.
subfiles.summary: Panama telegram 836: the remaining seized Japanese archives were moved into the American Embassy Office Building on September 7.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 836 from Panama on Transfer of Seized Japanese Archives

subfiles.about: Reports a conversation with the Soviet Chargé d'Affaires in Mexico regarding Japanese archives, intervened property, and reparations.
subfiles.summary: Messersmith told the Soviet Chargé that Allied action on Japanese archives was suspended; they also discussed enemy assets, which Latin American republics must use for reparations.
subfiles.title: Letter and Memorandum of Conversation on Soviet Discussions regarding Japanese Property in Mexico
subfiles.to: John Willard Carrigan (Chief, Division of Mexican Affairs)

subfiles.about: Records the withdrawal and charging out of document file 894.414/9-1145 in August 1960.
subfiles.summary: Charge-out card DS-1033 for file 894.414/9-1145, charged out August 18, 1960.
subfiles.title: Charge-Out Record for File 894.414/9-1145

subfiles.about: Reviews the history and complications of obtaining custody of Japanese overseas archives pending MacArthur's orders in Tokyo.
subfiles.from: Frederick B. Lyon (FC) and Oscar S. Straus (FC)
subfiles.summary: Lyon and Straus outline the impasse: Japan said Potsdam did not cover overseas archives and MacArthur deferred orders; they ask whether missions should wait and whether Japan will have future diplomatic representation.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Dilemma Over Custody of Japanese Diplomatic Archives and Property

subfiles.about: Reports postponing a Soviet proposal for immediate tripartite takeover of Japanese archives in Colombia.
subfiles.summary: Bogota telegram 1185: the Soviet Minister proposed immediate tripartite custody of Japanese archives; Wiley, backed by Britain, postponed action pending instructions and welcomes acting as sole joint custodian.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1185 from Bogota on Soviet Pressure for Joint Action on Archives

subfiles.about: Discusses coordinating with the British and OSS to prevent the destruction of Japanese archives in Bangkok.
subfiles.from: Abbott Low Moffat (SEA) and Oscar S. Straus (FC)
subfiles.summary: Straus and Moffat: Thailand could transfer Japanese archives to a protecting power if it severs relations; with British forces in Bangkok, OSS will contact the British to prevent destruction.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation on Japanese Archives in Bangkok

subfiles.about: Urges the State Department to seize records of the Japanese Black Dragon Society to identify members in the United States.
subfiles.from: Representative Gerald W. Landis (House of Representatives)
subfiles.summary: Representative Landis urges Byrnes to have occupation authorities seize Black Dragon Society files to help locate members in the US.
subfiles.title: Letter from Representative Gerald W. Landis on Black Dragon Society Files

subfiles.about: Informs Congressman Landis that Black Dragon Society files were reportedly destroyed, but military search continues.
subfiles.summary: Acheson tells Landis society members claimed their files were destroyed by air raids or burned; the Army is searching but found nothing.
subfiles.title: Letter to Representative Gerald W. Landis regarding Black Dragon Society Files
subfiles.to: Representative Gerald W. Landis (House of Representatives)

subfiles.about: Recommends keeping overseas Japanese archives in abeyance pending MacArthur's orders and examines future Japanese representation.
subfiles.from: Joseph W. Ballantine (Director, Office of Far Eastern Affairs - FE)
subfiles.summary: Ballantine advises holding overseas Japanese archives in abeyance pending MacArthur's orders, with a circular telling missions to desist; no policy yet on postwar Japanese diplomatic representation, which Britain would eliminate.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Diplomatic Representation and Overseas Japanese Archives
subfiles.to: Frederick B. Lyon (Chief, Division of Foreign Activity Correlation - CON)

subfiles.about: Informs Embassy Ankara that a definitive statement on Japanese archives is impossible and advises leaving custody with the Swiss.
subfiles.summary: Acheson tells Ankara no definitive decision on Japanese archives is possible now; the Swiss Legation should keep custody.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 920 to Ankara on Custody of Japanese Archives in Turkey

subfiles.about: Records briefing George Atcheson, Jr., on the urgency of having MacArthur order the surrender of overseas Japanese archives.
subfiles.summary: Straus urged Atcheson, leaving as MacArthur's adviser, to press MacArthur to direct Japan to order overseas missions to surrender archives; Atcheson promised to raise it.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation with George Atcheson, Jr., on Japanese Archives Problem

subfiles.about: Recommends assigning an OSS representative attached to the Legation to examine seized Japanese archives in Beirut.
subfiles.summary: Beirut telegram 286: Wadsworth sees no objection to having the OSS representative on his staff examine the Japanese archives.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 286 from Beirut on Assigning OSS Representative to Examine Archives

subfiles.about: Authorizes the Beirut Legation to have an OSS representative examine Japanese archives and submit an intelligence report.
subfiles.summary: Acheson authorizes Wadsworth to have an OSS representative or other staff examine the Beirut archives and submit a report with hectograph copies to Foreign Activity Correlation.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 280 to Beirut Authorizing Examination of Japanese Archives
